note: A synthetic client (Slice 129 worked example). Not a real company.
problem: Our credit scoring model predicted a default rate of 2.5% for last year's loans, but 3.5% actually defaulted.

answers.common.decision: Whether the model can stay in use; the validation opinion is signed by our head of model risk, who is independent of the model's owner.
answers.common.deadline: The annual model review in six weeks.
answers.common.audience: The head of model risk and the model owner.
answers.common.materials: Last year we approved 12,000 loans using the model, with an average balance of $25,000. Our tolerance for the gap between predicted and actual default rates is 0.5 percentage points.
answers.finance-modeling.purpose: Test the model's predicted defaults against actual defaults.
answers.finance-modeling.data: Last year's loan-level predictions and outcomes from the model owner, in US dollars.
